analysis:
Examined all supplied CI excerpts and the complete changed-range map. .github/workflows/ci.yml:53-64 adds macOS routing lanes; head lines 232-234, 477-479, 675-677, 878-880 and 1010-1012 replace fixed Blacksmith runners with route outputs and add route dependencies. The BASE GPU/focused jobs at 1053-1168 establish their previous fixed-runner behavior; their HEAD replacements are identified by the range map but not replayed here. Test commands, classifier conditions, cache-write restrictions, checkout credential settings and artifact handling in the supplied source are unchanged. BASE lines 1170-1202 show the selected-lane success/intentional-skip gate, outside the changed ranges. No independently supported control removal or gate bypass was found.
The new execution location matters because providers are adversarial (ADV-001): routed Macs execute PR-controlled code and produce provider/native test evidence, build caches on eligible pushes, and artifacts consumed by the summary job (head 526-537). Integration must examine .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml and its provisioning implementation for runner authenticity, host/VM isolation, clean job state, credential exposure, cache separation and teardown, including fork PRs and cancellation. These controls are outside this batch, not demonstrably absent. Relevant contracts include A-019/TB-013 and signed-build/qualification integrity A-011, A-017, T-054; test success alone must not become attestation or qualification of an adversarial host. No serving authorization, encryption, prompt/cache scoping (T-041), billing or native inference implementation changes are visible. Selected canonical definitions, not every full definition, were supplied. Remaining runner-boundary uncertainty requires integration review; this local result does not establish the routed execution environment is safe.
